title: Covering index for a frequent query
claim: A covering index holds every column the query needs, so the database never touches the table.
Filter columns first, then sort columns, then the selected ones. Costs space and write speed.
verdict: Confirmed, with a trade-off. The covering index (date_c INCLUDE function, version, duration) turned the top-APIs
query into an index-only scan: {t:date_index} to {t:covering} ({x:date_index/covering}). Price: 299 MB vs 108 MB
for the plain date index, and 10,000 inserts took {pct:insert_after/insert_before} time. Worth it for a
dashboard query that runs constantly, not for every query.
